current_scope: Research-only analytic/manufactured dummy-SWAP coupling oracles against live MODFLOW6 6.8.0.
current_bounded_findings: A shared phreatic head and a true finite-resistance q-link are different physical coupling families.
Physical storage ownership must be declared exactly once. Consistent repartition is invariant; duplicated storage has a predictable signature.
A response tangent HCOF is not by itself a physical storage coefficient or a physical interface conductance.
Depth-varying and nonlinear storage must be checked against integrated water volume, not only a local derivative.
Head-dependent ET and drain derivatives are sink-response tangents with different physical ownership from storage.
A shared groundwater head can be a valid shared state while remaining an incomplete state descriptor when the unsaturated column has internal memory.
Forcing order is irrelevant in the memoryless linear control but becomes physically relevant in the transparent memory surrogate without violating mass conservation.
Linear N:1 aggregation is the area-weighted sum of cell response terms and is permutation invariant. This does not establish heterogeneous Richards transferability.
MODFLOW subsystem convergence, external coupled residual closure and physical mass closure are distinct acceptance objects.
DSW05 shows that an extremely strict IMS inner residual certificate can remain false even when the analytic head is reached to machine precision.

DSW09 separates two numerical effects. MODERATE delta-bar-delta under-relaxation changes the reanchor trajectory; after removing it, near-root strict residual certification can still fail when the remaining affine residual exceeds rclose but no useful floating-point head correction is available.
Fresh-solve success can depend on starting distance from the affine root. It must not be interpreted automatically as proof of hidden prepared-solve linear-solver state.

Bit-exact transfer of accepted state matters for substep/restart oracles. Text-formatted initial-head serialization produced a false DSW15 mass defect that disappeared when X and XOLD were set exactly through XMI.
Equal-and-opposite internal transfers conserve the complete coupled inventory in both directions; a transfer into groundwater is not automatically net recharge to the complete system.

Storage sensitivity and finite-resistance q-link conductance have different limiting signatures. Storage controls head response to net volume, whereas q-link conductance controls head separation and internal exchange between distinct storages.
Numerical convergence is not scientific acceptance: duplicate storage, a wrong storage-response sign and a reversed forcing sign all converge to deterministic but physically wrong states.

A five-window manufactured trajectory with unequal timesteps, explicit memory, lateral input, ET and drainage closes both window and cumulative mass ledgers to machine precision when state continuation is explicit.
unresolved_scientific_questions: How does real SWAP q_u/u decompose into physical storage change, external/sink flux response and numerical tangent under the intended shared-domain ownership?
Which real SWAP internal states beyond phreatic head are required to predict the next corrector response over a coupling window?
Under which real hydrological regimes should the SWAP-MODFLOW connection be treated as shared-state h-link, explicit q-link, or another boundary-exchange formulation?
unresolved_numerical_questions: What production tolerance envelope should jointly govern MODFLOW subsystem convergence, coupling residual and mass conservation without demanding unattainable floating-point residuals?
Should external reanchoring use MODFLOW nonlinear under-relaxation history unchanged, disable/reset that acceleration, or move coupling acceleration explicitly to the outer coupling level?
How do these one-cell observations scale to multi-cell mixed-topology production windows?
next_safe_steps: Keep all production F-GC code unchanged.

Reconcile the exact F-GC33/F-GC49 response contract against the closed dummy taxonomy: identify what q_ref, u/HCOF and RHS represent mathematically and which terms are physical storage, physical sinks/boundaries, or numerical tangent only.

Select controlled real-SWAP/FMR fixtures with independently auditable water ledgers and capture committed origin state, trial head, q_u/u or equivalent response terms, corrector flux and accepted mass change over one coupling window.
For those fixtures, test whether the real response is consistent with a shared-state h-link, a finite-resistance q-link, or neither; do not choose a coupling family by analogy alone.
Then extend the same audit to multiple SWAP tiles mapped N:1 while keeping heterogeneous-transferability claims separate from the algebraic aggregation proof.
